articles.title: OpenAI Launches GPT-5 Turbo with Native Multimodal Reasoning Across Code, Video, and Audio
articles.summary: OpenAI released GPT-5 Turbo, featuring deeply integrated multimodal reasoning that can jointly process video streams, audio, and code repositories in a single context window of up to 1 million tokens. Early benchmarks show a 38% improvement over GPT-5 on complex software engineering tasks and near-human performance on graduate-level scientific reasoning. The model also introduces a new 'chain-of-tools' capability that autonomously orchestrates API calls and tool use without explicit prompting.

articles.title: Google DeepMind's Gemini Ultra 2 Achieves State-of-the-Art on Mathematical Olympiad Problems
articles.summary: DeepMind announced that Gemini Ultra 2 solved 89% of International Mathematical Olympiad problems from the past decade, a significant leap from the 68% achieved by its predecessor earlier this year. The system combines advanced formal reasoning with a novel self-verification loop that checks proofs against the Lean 4 theorem prover in real time. Researchers say this marks a milestone toward AI systems capable of genuine mathematical discovery rather than pattern matching.

articles.title: Boston Dynamics Unveils Atlas Gen-3 with Dexterous Manipulation and Real-Time Adaptive Gait
articles.summary: Boston Dynamics revealed the third generation of its electric Atlas humanoid robot, featuring new five-fingered hands with 22 degrees of freedom per hand and tactile sensing at each fingertip. The robot demonstrated assembling automotive wiring harnesses in a factory pilot with Hyundai, completing tasks previously requiring human dexterity. A new real-time adaptive gait controller allows Atlas Gen-3 to traverse unstructured terrain including loose gravel and stairs while carrying up to 25 kg payloads.

articles.title: Figure and BMW Expand Humanoid Robot Deployment to Three Additional Manufacturing Plants
articles.summary: Figure Inc. announced that its Figure 02 humanoid robots will be deployed to three additional BMW manufacturing plants in Germany and the US following a successful 12-month pilot in Spartanburg, South Carolina. The robots now handle bin picking, parts inspection, and ergonomically challenging above-head assembly tasks, reportedly reducing workplace injury claims by 34% on pilot lines. BMW plans to scale to over 500 units by mid-2027, making it one of the largest humanoid deployments in automotive history.

articles.title: Anthropic Introduces 'Constitutional Classifiers' to Defend Against Jailbreaks in Production AI Systems
articles.summary: Anthropic published a technical report detailing Constitutional Classifiers, a new safety architecture that reduces successful jailbreak rates on Claude models to under 0.2% across a battery of over 50,000 adversarial prompts. The system trains lightweight classifier heads on synthetically generated attack-defense pairs derived from the model's own constitution. The approach is model-agnostic and Anthropic has open-sourced the training framework, inviting the industry to adopt it as a shared safety standard.

articles.title: TSMC Begins Volume Production of 1.4nm Process Node Ahead of Schedule
articles.summary: TSMC confirmed that its N1.4 process node has entered high-volume manufacturing at its Fab 20 facility in Hsinchu, roughly one quarter ahead of the originally projected timeline. The node delivers a 20% performance gain and 30% power reduction over N2, with backside power delivery and gate-all-around nanosheet transistors as standard. Initial customers include Apple and Nvidia, with chips expected in consumer and data center products by early 2027.

articles.title: EU AI Act Enforcement Begins: First Wave of Compliance Deadlines Hit Enterprise Providers
articles.summary: The European Union's AI Act entered its broadest enforcement phase on September 15, requiring all high-risk AI system providers operating in the EU to register in the bloc's centralized AI database and submit conformity assessments. Several major US tech firms including Microsoft, Google, and Meta disclosed compliance costs exceeding €200 million each, while a number of smaller startups announced they will geo-fence EU users rather than meet the requirements. Legal experts expect the first enforcement actions by year-end.

articles.title: Neuralink Receives FDA Clearance for Second-Generation Brain-Computer Interface with Wireless Charging
articles.summary: Neuralink announced FDA clearance for its N2 brain-computer interface implant, which doubles the electrode count to 2,048 channels and introduces wireless inductive charging, eliminating the need for any percutaneous connectors. The second-generation device also features on-chip spike sorting using a custom neuromorphic processor, reducing data transmission bandwidth by 90%. Expanded clinical trials for patients with quadriplegia and ALS are set to begin in Q1 2027 across five US medical centers.
